title: Overhaul reservation & burst policy and isolate noisy tenants after capacity incident
creator: Asha Kulkarni
description: Post-incident workstream created after a capacity storm on 2026-03-07 that caused elevated p95/p99 latencies and a cascade of soft evictions in a Dedicated cluster. This ticket consolidates experiments, proposed code changes, and an operational checklist to: (1) isolate noisy tenants faster, (2) recalibrate reservations to reduce steady-state under/over-allocation, and (3) redesign the burst credit system to avoid long tail exhaustion. Goal: implement safe mitigations and a staged rollout with synthetic canaries before the next maintenance window.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-07 at 03:14 UTC a tenant spike combined with a cache-amplifying workload caused sustained KV cache churn and ballooning worker queues. Autoscaler did not trigger in time due to reservation accounting lag; burst credits were rapidly consumed by a small set of tenants, causing soft evictions for unrelated tenants. P95 increased from 80ms to 1.8s; error rates for generation requests rose from 0.2% to 3.6% for the affected cluster for ~42 minutes.
timeline_highlights: 03:14 UTC - sudden tenant request rate increase, queue depth grew on pool-A
03:18 UTC - KV cache eviction rate spikes; cache hit ratio drops 46% -> 12%
03:24 UTC - tenant burst credits depleted for top noisy tenant; scheduler began soft evictions
03:56 UTC - mitigation applied: manual tenant fencing and reservation reassign; tail latency started returning to baseline
04:00 UTC - incident declared resolved at 04:00 after reservation rebalance and traffic shaping
root_causes: Reservation accounting has a 90s aggregation window leading to delayed autoscaler decisions
Burst-credit model is time-agnostic and allows large, rapid bursts to exhaust credits without gradual decay
KV cache eviction policy prefers global recency which amplified hot-key churn when a tenant replayed short sequences
No fast detection path for 'cache-dominant' noisy workloads in cluster telemetry
findings: High-volume short-sequence workloads can cause disproportionate KV memory churn due to current per-block eviction heuristics
Reservation estimator is tuned to smooth variance at cost of slower reaction to sudden sustained increases
Burst accounting lacks a per-tenant adaptive decay; current static bucket parameters create cliff-edge exhaustions
Operational runbooks allowed manual tenant fencing but lacked an automated probe that would have isolated the noisy tenant earlier
decisions: Implement a dual-timescale reservation estimator: fast-path (5s window) for autoscaler triggers + slow-path (5m window) for long-term sizing
Replace hard-cliff burst exhaustion with a graded throttle that preserves low-rate requests (control-plane and health checks) while shedding heavy token producers
Introduce cache-fairness knobs with tenant-weighted eviction scoring to prevent single-tenant hot-key replay from invalidating global KV state
Roll out changes behind a feature flag with a canary pipeline using synthetic tenant traffic and graduated ramping

acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler responds to a sustained 3x request spike within 30s with appropriate capacity suggestion or soft-fence action
Burst-throttle prevents full credit depletion for any tenant within a 60s sustained burst scenario while ensuring health-check/control-plane traffic remains unthrottled
KV cache prototype reduces cross-tenant eviction for synthetic hot-replay by >= 60% in staging benchmarks
Canary run (3-day soak) shows p95 <= 120ms and error rate <= 0.5% under a mixed workload that previously triggered the incident
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: fast-path reservation may oscillate on bursty workloads - Mitigation: introduce hysteresis and require sustained 3-sample confirmation before scaling actions
Risk: tenant-weighted cache could starve low-volume tenants - Mitigation: floor allocation and canary monitor for fairness metrics
Risk: rollout changes could interact with older dedicated pools - Mitigation: target a single non-customer-facing staging cluster first, then pilot customers with opt-in flag
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Lab: run KV eviction prototype and graded burst-throttle against synthetic harness (2 engineers, 1 week)
Phase 1 - Staging Canary: enable feature-flagged changes on staging pool-A, run 72h soak with synthetic tenants and production shadow for comparison
Phase 2 - Pilot: enable on one Dedicated customer pool with opt-in, monitor 7 days, rollback window 2 hours
Phase 3 - Gradual rollout: 10% -> 33% -> 100% of dedicated pools with daily monitoring and rollback gates
testing_plan: Unit and integration tests for graded burst-throttle including edge cases for very small bursts
End-to-end soak with synthetic harness that includes cache-amplifying replay, high-concurrency short sequences, and control-plane traffic
Chaos test: simulate delayed reservation telemetry and verify autoscaler fast-path still triggers safe actions
Performance benchmarks: measure p50/p95/p99 and cost delta with reservation fast-path enabled
